key_insight: A modular concert-editing framework combines musical activity, visible instruments, image sharpness and beat timing to choose camera views. Its interpretable scoring model evaluates views over complete shot intervals, rather than isolated moments.
problem_solved: Editing multi-camera concerts requires balancing which musicians are active, which camera views look good and when cuts fit the music.
method: Extract instrument activity from multitrack audio and identify visible instruments and image sharpness in camera footage.
Use beat-based timing to organize shot intervals and an interpretable scoring model to assess candidate views.
Select cameras probabilistically; evaluate components and explore expert feedback on a four-camera concert.
impact: The framework offers practitioners an interpretable way to combine audio and visual signals for automated editing. The supplied abstract reports mixed evaluation results but is truncated, so strong performance claims are not supported.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multitrack audio and camera footage → feature extraction → scoring → camera selection.
Beat-aligned timeline showing instrument activity and selected camera shots.
Four-camera grid annotated with visible instruments and sharpness scores.
Score breakdown illustrating how musical relevance and visual quality influence view selection.
paper_title: Multimodal Concert Video Editing: System Design and Exploratory Evaluation
paper_authors: Lennart Schiweck, Adrian Kempf, Michelle Retig, Moritz Feucht, Tim Mangliers
